To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of DA on memory are larger at encoding than at retrieval, that DA has a larger effect on memory when a secondary task is performed at the same time as the memory task than when it follows the memory task, and that the effects of a secondary task at encoding are sensitive to the relative emphasis placed on the two tasks, whereas the effects at retrieval are not.
the effects of dividedattention (DA) atencoding and retrieval are different.

divided attention (DA), at encoding, has large effects on memory performance and small effects on response latencies (RTs) in both free recall and recognition, but at retrieval, DA has small effects on memory performance but large effects on RT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of divided and selective attention on the encoding and retrieval of verbal material.
the effects of attention on encoding and on retrieval.
the effects of divided-attention (DA) on encoding and retrieval in memory.

the results from the present experiments indicate that the processes involved in encoding and retrieval are similar but not identical.
the effects of DA on retrieval processes are much smaller than those observed on encoding processes.
divided attention (DA), at encoding or retrieval, affects memory processes in a similar manner, but that the effects are more pronounced at encoding than at retrieval.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results are compatible with an interactive view of the processes of encoding and retrieval.
divided attention (DA), at encoding, affects the encoding process, but that at retrieval it affects the retrieval process.
we have found a dissociation of encoding and retrieval processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
encoding and retrieval processes can be dissociated, and that the two processes are differentially affected by manipulations of attentional demands.
the effects of divided and focused attention on memory performance are not identical.
